newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Veba oil business drives H1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Veba oil business drives H1 earnings.

text.p: German diversified utility giant Veba AG said on Thursday it expected 1997 full-year earnings to rise at least as fast as in the first half, after reporting double-digit half-year earnings growth.
The group said the first-half earnings increase was driven by growth in its oil unit, Veba Oel, and in its trading, transport and services business.
Veba's group net profit in the first six months of 1997 was 1.01 billion marks ($534.8 million), up from 896 million marks.

"The figures were in line with our expectations and the company said they expect similar earnings growth rates for the rest of the year," Winfried Mathes, utilities analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said.

Higher oil refining margins, price increases and the weakness of the mark were the main engines for growth in the oil business, which increased sales to 9.6 billion marks from 8.4 billion marks in the first half, Veba said.
"Refining was up, petrochemicals were up and the dollar helped boost its upstream business," Mathes said.
However, some analysts were worried about falling returns in the group's chemicals' business, where sales grew slightly to 5.6 billion marks in the first half from 5.4 billion.

"The figures show that returns are declining on the group's chemicals business, despite the programme of rigorous cost-cutting at Veba, the group barely managed double-digit growth," one utilities analyst said.
"We see returns on capital declining in the second half of the year as the group starts consolidating its acquisitions," he added.

One of Veba's big buys during the first six months was a 36.4 percent of the German chemical group Degussa AG, which is still awaiting cartel watchdog approval and which has met with mixed reactions from analysts.
"Our chemicals analysts are not overly excited by the Degussa acquisition. They like the company but don't see where the real points of integration lie," an analyst said.
Veba's core cash-generating business remains its electricity division, which saw sales increase 8.05 billion marks compared in the to 7.77 billion marks.

"Electricity prices remained stable, which is good news for Veba. The programme of cost-cutting by German utilities looks like it is going to end up in the pockets of the shareholders and as a result we overweight German utilities," said Peter Gyllenbaga, utilities analyst at CSFB in London.
Electricity prices are not expected to fall for the rest of the year, but Mathes said there could be small price falls in mid-to-late 1998.

Price-cutting has an important role to play in earnings growth in the electricity sector, as turnover rose only 3.6 percent to 8.048 billion marks in the first half, but earnings stood at around year-ago levels, Veba said.
"Returns are falling in its cyclical businesses, despite cost-cutting, and Veba is a bit more exposed to cyclical business than some of the other utilities," Gyllenbaga said.
Veba shares reacted positively to the figures and ended bourse trade up 3.30 marks, or three percent, to 112.60 marks, while the 30-share DAX index jumped 78.96 points or 1.82 percent to 4,414.35.
